title: Object Storage
summary: Object storage like S3 keeps trillions of files with eleven nines of durability by never trusting any single disk. Each object is split and erasure-coded into fragments spread across racks and data centres, so it survives several simultaneous failures while using far less space than full copies. A separate metadata service maps keys to fragments and makes writes visible atomically, and background processes constantly verify and repair data.

walkthrough.title: PUT an object
walkthrough.text: A client sends PUT /photos/cat.jpg with a SigV4-signed request. The front end authenticates it, checks bucket policy, and streams the body in.

walkthrough.title: Erasure-code across fault domains
walkthrough.text: The data is split into 8 data fragments plus 4 parity fragments (8+4) and written to 12 storage nodes in different racks and zones. Any 8 fragments can rebuild the object, so it survives 4 losses at 1.5× storage cost instead of 3× for copies.

walkthrough.title: Commit metadata
walkthrough.text: Only once enough fragments are durable is the key → fragment-location map committed in the metadata service. From that moment every reader sees the new object (strong read-after-write consistency).

walkthrough.title: GET the object
walkthrough.text: A read looks up the key's metadata, fetches fragments from the fastest nodes in parallel, reconstructs the object, and verifies its checksum before streaming it.

walkthrough.title: Multipart upload for large files
walkthrough.text: A 50 GB video is uploaded as many 100 MB parts in parallel and retried individually. A final CompleteMultipartUpload stitches them into one object atomically.

walkthrough.title: Scrub and repair
walkthrough.text: Background scrubbers re-read fragments to catch silent corruption (bit rot). When a disk or node dies, the repair service rebuilds its fragments elsewhere from the survivors.

walkthrough.title: Lifecycle and replication
walkthrough.text: Lifecycle rules move old objects to colder, cheaper tiers or delete them, and cross-region replication copies objects to another region for disaster recovery.

data.label: Client (S3 API)
responsibilities: Uploads and downloads objects by bucket and key.
Uses multipart uploads and parallel range GETs for big objects.
Verifies integrity with checksums.

failureModes.impact: Sensitive data exposed to the internet.
failureModes.mitigation: Block public access by default; policy scanning.
Lifecycle rule to abort incomplete uploads after N days.

data.label: API Front End
responsibilities: Authenticates requests and enforces access policies.
Encodes and decodes erasure-coded fragments.
Rate-limits per prefix to protect the system.

failureModes.scenario: Hot prefix (all keys start with a date)
failureModes.mitigation: Automatic prefix partitioning; spread key names.
Nothing visible until commit; client retries the part.

data.label: Metadata Service

input.name: Commit / lookup
input.type: bucket/key → version, size, ETag, fragment map

responsibilities: Maps every key to where its fragments live.
Makes writes atomic and immediately visible.
Serves LIST by key prefix in sorted order.

failureModes.impact: Keys in that range cannot be read or written.

failureModes.scenario: Huge LIST of a billion-key bucket
failureModes.mitigation: Paginated listing; inventory reports for bulk analysis.

data.label: Storage Nodes
responsibilities: Stores fragments on many disks in independent failure domains.
Serves fragment reads in parallel.
Reports disk health for proactive replacement.

failureModes.mitigation: Place at most a few fragments per rack and zone.
Read extra fragments and use the first 8 to arrive (hedged reads).

data.label: Scrubber & Repair
responsibilities: Detects silent corruption before it accumulates.
Rebuilds lost fragments quickly to restore full redundancy.
Prioritises objects that have lost the most fragments.

failureModes.impact: Durability erodes; data loss risk grows.
failureModes.mitigation: Capacity for repair bandwidth; prioritise most-degraded objects.
Throttle repair adaptively; spread it across many nodes.

data.label: Lifecycle & Replication

input.name: Rules
input.type: After 30 d → infrequent; 365 d → archive; replicate prefix

responsibilities: Moves data to cheaper tiers as it ages.
Expires objects per retention rules.
Copies objects to another region asynchronously.

failureModes.mitigation: Versioning plus object lock for critical buckets.

failureModes.impact: Recent objects missing after a regional failover.
failureModes.mitigation: Replication time control (SLA) and lag monitoring.

data.label: Second Region

output.name: DR reads
output.type: Serve traffic if the primary region fails

responsibilities: Holds an independent copy for disaster recovery.
Serves nearby readers with lower latency.
Meets data-residency requirements.

failureModes.mitigation: Versioning and delete-marker policies in the replica.
